description: One of the largest land predators ever, with a massive skull, bone-crushing teeth the size of bananas, and surprisingly tiny two-fingered arms. It ruled the floodplains of western North America at the very end of the age of dinosaurs.
interestingFacts: Its bite was the strongest of any land animal ever measured — over 5 tonnes of force.
Despite its size, some scientists think it could jog at around 20 km/h.
A famous specimen named Sue is the most complete T. rex ever found.

description: A tank-like plant-eater with two long brow horns, a shorter nose horn, and a huge bony neck frill. It lived alongside Tyrannosaurus rex and could defend itself against it.
interestingFacts: Its skull could be over 2.5 metres long — one of the largest of any land animal.
It sheared through tough plants with hundreds of teeth stacked in batteries.
Fossils show healed horn injuries, evidence of real battles.

description: A fast, feathered hunter about the size of a turkey — much smaller than in the movies. It used a large sickle-shaped claw on each foot to pin down its prey in the deserts of Mongolia.
interestingFacts: A famous fossil preserves one locked in combat with a Protoceratops.
Quill knobs on its arm bones prove it had feathers.
Its sickle claw could grow to about 6.5 cm long.

description: Instantly recognisable by the two rows of big bony plates along its back and the four long tail spikes it swung at attackers. Its brain was famously tiny — about the size of a walnut.
interestingFacts: The spiky tail weapon is nicknamed the 'thagomizer'.
Its back plates may have flushed with blood to change colour.
An Allosaurus fossil has a wound matching a Stegosaurus tail spike.

imageAttribution: DataBase Center for Life Science (DBCLS), Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0
description: A giraffe-like giant whose front legs were longer than its back legs, tilting its long neck up to browse treetops other dinosaurs couldn't reach — up to 9 metres above the ground.
interestingFacts: It's named 'arm lizard' because of those long front legs.
It swallowed leaves whole — no chewing — and let its stomach do the work.
It was the first dinosaur shown in the movie Jurassic Park.

description: One of the longest dinosaurs known from good skeletons, built like a suspension bridge with a whip-like tail longer than its neck. Casts of its skeleton stand in museums all over the world.
interestingFacts: Its tail had about 80 vertebrae and may have cracked like a whip.
It likely stripped leaves from branches with comb-like front teeth.
Steel tycoon Andrew Carnegie funded the famous specimen 'Dippy'.

description: Longer than T. rex, with a crocodile-like snout for catching fish and a spectacular 1.7-metre sail on its back. It's the best candidate we have for a swimming dinosaur.
interestingFacts: The original fossils were destroyed in a WWII bombing raid on Munich.
New fossils show it had a tall paddle-like tail for swimming.
Its nostrils sat high on its skull, handy for a life around water.

description: A living fortress covered in bony armour plates, with a huge club of solid bone at the end of its tail that could swing hard enough to break a predator's leg.
interestingFacts: Even its eyelids had bony armour.
The tail club could weigh more than 20 kilograms.
It kept its soft belly close to the ground — flipping it over was the only way in.

description: The top predator of the Late Jurassic, with short horns above its eyes and a mouth that opened extremely wide. It hunted the great plant-eaters of its time, possibly in groups.
interestingFacts: More than 46 individuals were found in one Utah quarry alone.
It may have used its upper jaw like a hatchet to slash prey.
It lived 80 million years before T. rex — they never met.

description: A duck-billed dinosaur with a long, curved tube of bone sweeping back from its head. The hollow crest worked like a trombone, letting it make deep honking calls across the herd.
interestingFacts: Scientists have recreated its call with computer models — a low foghorn sound.
The crest could be over 1 metre long.
It could walk on two legs or four.

description: A heavyweight cousin of Diplodocus with a thicker, more powerful build. For a century it was better known by its other name — Brontosaurus, the 'thunder lizard'.
interestingFacts: Its neck bones were unusually wide and strong — maybe for neck-wrestling contests.
A single thigh bone can be taller than an adult human.
The Brontosaurus name was recently argued back to life for a close relative.

description: One of the very first dinosaurs ever named, famous for the sharp thumb spikes it used like daggers. Dozens of complete skeletons were found together deep in a Belgian coal mine.
interestingFacts: Early scientists thought its thumb spike was a horn on its nose.
It was only the second creature ever called a 'dinosaur'.
It could grip branches with a bendy little finger.

description: The famous head-butting dinosaur, with a domed skull roof up to 25 centimetres thick surrounded by a crown of bony knobs. Rivals may have rammed each other like bighorn sheep.
interestingFacts: Its skull dome was 20 times thicker than a human skull.
Some skulls show healed injuries from head-on collisions.
Young ones had flat heads that domed as they grew.

description: A South American sprinter with two devil-like horns over its eyes and arms even stubbier than T. rex's. Its huge leg muscles made it one of the fastest big predators ever.
interestingFacts: Skin impressions show it was covered in rows of scaly bumps.
Its arms were so short they had almost no use at all.
It may have sprinted at over 50 km/h.

description: An early predator wearing two thin, rounded crests on its head like a double mohawk. The real animal was much bigger than the movies show — and there's no evidence it spat venom.
interestingFacts: It was the largest land predator of its time in North America.
The movie frill and venom were pure fiction.
Its fossils were found on Navajo Nation land in Arizona.

description: A chicken-sized speedster that chased lizards and insects across Jurassic lagoon islands. For over a century it held the record as the smallest known dinosaur.
interestingFacts: One fossil still has a whole lizard inside its stomach.
It lived on the same islands where Archaeopteryx flew.
Its name means 'elegant jaw' for its delicate skull.

description: The raptor that changed science: its build convinced researchers that dinosaurs were fast, warm-blooded and bird-like. The Jurassic Park 'Velociraptors' were really modelled on it.
interestingFacts: Its study kick-started the 'dinosaur renaissance' of the 1960s.
Several skeletons found together hint that it hunted in packs.
Its killing claw stayed razor-sharp by never touching the ground.

description: Possibly the largest land animal that ever lived — as heavy as ten elephants. It's known from just a few colossal bones, including vertebrae taller than a person.
interestingFacts: A single backbone vertebra measures 1.6 metres tall.
Hatchlings the size of a cat grew 25,000 times heavier as adults.
It was discovered by a rancher who thought a bone was petrified wood.

description: The dinosaur with the longest claws of any animal ever — up to a metre each. Despite the terrifying scythes, this pot-bellied giant used them to hook leafy branches, not prey.
interestingFacts: Scientists first thought its claws belonged to a giant turtle.
Its claws could reach 1 metre — the longest of any known animal.
It was a plant-eater descended from meat-eating ancestors.

description: The punk rocker of horned dinosaurs: four to six long spikes fanned out from its frill, with a half-metre horn on its nose. The display probably impressed rivals and mates alike.
interestingFacts: Its nose horn alone could be 57 centimetres long.
Huge bone beds show its herds numbered in the hundreds.
Each individual's frill spikes were arranged slightly differently.

description: A duck-billed dinosaur with a tall, rounded crest like an ancient Greek helmet. Air looping through the hollow crest gave each animal its own deep, resonant voice.
interestingFacts: One fossil preserved skin impressions over much of the body.
Its crest shape changed with age and differed between sexes.
It had up to 600 tiny teeth for grinding plants.

description: A Jurassic predator with a blade-like horn on its nose, small horns over its eyes, and a row of little armour plates down its back — unique among meat-eaters.
interestingFacts: It's the only known meat-eater with bony armour along its spine.
Its teeth were enormous for its body size.
It competed with the bigger Allosaurus for the same prey.

description: A fish-hunting cousin of Spinosaurus found in an English clay pit, named for the huge 31-centimetre claw on each thumb. Its crocodile-like jaws held nearly a hundred teeth.
interestingFacts: Fish scales and a young Iguanodon were found in its stomach.
It was discovered by an amateur fossil hunter, a plumber named William Walker.
It's one of the most complete big predators ever found in Britain.

description: A sheep-sized early relative of Triceratops with a bony frill but no big horns. Whole herds, nests and even eggs were found preserved in Mongolia's Gobi Desert sands.
interestingFacts: Its skeletons may have inspired the legend of the griffin.
A famous fossil shows one frozen mid-fight with a Velociraptor.
Dozens were found in every size from hatchling to adult.

description: A slender, fast-running early predator with a long neck and tail and needle-sharp teeth. One of the earliest dinosaurs, it hunted small animals in herds across the deserts of ancient North America.
interestingFacts: Hundreds of skeletons were found jumbled together at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
It was one of the earliest true dinosaurs, from near the dawn of the age of dinosaurs.
A Coelophysis skull flew aboard Space Shuttle Endeavour in 1998.

description: A large early plant-eater that reared up on its hind legs to browse high foliage. An ancestor-type of the giant long-necked sauropods, it was one of the first big dinosaurs.
interestingFacts: It was one of the very first dinosaurs ever scientifically named, back in the 1830s.
Dozens of skeletons have been dug from European 'dinosaur graveyards'.
It walked on two legs but had a long neck and small head like its giant sauropod cousins.

description: A stocky long-necked giant with a short, boxy skull and large nostrils above its eyes. It was the most common sauropod of the Jurassic plains of western North America.
interestingFacts: Its name means 'chambered lizard' after the hollow, air-filled chambers in its backbone.
It is the most complete and commonly found sauropod from the Morrison Formation.
Its spoon-shaped teeth were strong enough to chew tough plants whole.

description: A colossal Chinese sauropod famous for having one of the longest necks of any animal that has ever lived — almost half of its entire body length.
interestingFacts: Its neck could reach up to about 15 metres — the longest neck known in the animal kingdom.
The neck alone made up nearly half of its total body length.
It was named after Mamen Brook in China, where the first bones were found.

description: A huge duck-billed dinosaur with hundreds of grinding teeth packed into its jaws. It lived in vast herds right up to the very end of the age of dinosaurs, alongside T. rex.
interestingFacts: Its jaws held a 'dental battery' of up to a thousand teeth for grinding tough plants.
Mummified specimens have preserved its skin texture and even a fleshy head crest.
It lived side by side with Tyrannosaurus rex and was likely its prey.

description: A duck-billed plant-eater crowned with a hollow, hatchet-shaped crest on its head. The crest was filled with air tubes that may have let it trumpet loud calls.
interestingFacts: Its hollow head crest was shaped like a hatchet or axe blade.
Air passages inside the crest may have worked like a trumpet to make sounds.
It was named in honour of Canadian palaeontologist Lawrence Lambe.

description: An African cousin of Stegosaurus with a double row of plates near the shoulders that gave way to a fearsome set of long, sharp spikes down its back and tail.
interestingFacts: Unlike Stegosaurus, most of its back and tail were lined with spikes rather than plates.
It had extra spikes jutting out from its shoulders or hips for defence.
Its fossils were found in Tanzania, in East Africa.

description: A duck-billed dinosaur whose nesting grounds revealed that it cared for its babies. Whole colonies nested together, tending eggs and feeding hatchlings in the nest.
interestingFacts: Its name means 'good mother lizard' — the first clear proof dinosaurs cared for their young.
Fossil nesting colonies were found with eggs, babies and adults together.
It is the official state fossil of Montana, USA.

description: A feathered, parrot-beaked dinosaur that was wrongly accused of stealing eggs. We now know the 'stolen' eggs were its own — it was actually sitting on its nest like a bird.
interestingFacts: It was named 'egg thief' by mistake — it was really protecting its own nest.
It had a toothless beak and a crest on its head, a bit like a cassowary.
Fossils show it brooded its eggs the same way modern birds do.

description: An ostrich-like dinosaur with a toothless beak, long legs and feathered arms. Built for speed, it could sprint away from predators across the open plains.
interestingFacts: It looked and ran much like a modern ostrich and may have reached 50–70 km/h.
Fossils show wing-like feathers on its arms even though it couldn't fly.
Its toothless beak suggests it ate plants, insects and small animals.

description: A crow-sized creature that is half dinosaur, half bird — with feathers and wings but also teeth, clawed fingers and a long bony tail. It is one of the most famous fossils ever found.
interestingFacts: It is often called the 'first bird' and links dinosaurs to modern birds.
It had feathers and wings like a bird but teeth and a bony tail like a dinosaur.
Its fossils were found in Germany just after Darwin published his theory of evolution.

description: A lighter, faster relative of T. rex that ruled Canada a few million years earlier. It had the same tiny arms and huge jaws, but a slimmer, speedier build.
interestingFacts: It was a smaller, older cousin of Tyrannosaurus rex.
A bonebed of 26 individuals hints that it may have hunted in packs.
Being lighter than T. rex, it was probably a faster runner.

description: A small, parrot-beaked plant-eater that was an early cousin of Triceratops — long before the great horned dinosaurs evolved. It is one of the best-known dinosaurs of all.
interestingFacts: Its parrot-like beak gives it the name 'parrot lizard'.
It was an early relative of the horned dinosaurs like Triceratops.
One superb fossil preserves bristles on its tail and even its camouflage colours.

description: The Asian cousin of T. rex and the top predator of Cretaceous Mongolia. It shared the same giant jaws and comically tiny two-fingered arms.
interestingFacts: It was the largest predator in Asia at the end of the age of dinosaurs.
It is the closest known relative of Tyrannosaurus rex.
Like T. rex, it had huge jaws but very short, small arms.

description: One of the largest meat-eating dinosaurs ever, with blade-like teeth serrated like a shark's. It prowled the rivers of North Africa alongside Spinosaurus.
interestingFacts: Its name means 'shark-toothed lizard' after its serrated, blade-like teeth.
It rivalled T. rex and Spinosaurus as one of the biggest land predators ever.
Its original fossils were destroyed when a museum was bombed in World War II.

description: A huge predator with tall spines along its back forming a low ridge or sail. It was the apex hunter of early Cretaceous North America.
interestingFacts: Tall spines along its backbone formed a muscular ridge down its back.
It was the top predator of its time and place in North America.
Fossil trackways seem to show it stalking a giant long-necked sauropod.

description: One of the strangest dinosaurs of all — a giant, humpbacked, duck-billed ostrich-dinosaur. For 50 years it was known only from its enormous 2.4-metre arms.
interestingFacts: For half a century it was a mystery known only from two gigantic arms.
Its arms were about 2.4 metres long — some of the largest of any predator.
The full skeleton revealed a bizarre humped back and a duck-like bill.

description: A giant feathered, beaked dinosaur as long as a bus — a super-sized relative of the little Oviraptor. It shows that some bird-like dinosaurs grew to enormous size.
interestingFacts: It was a bird-like beaked dinosaur that grew as big as a Tyrannosaurus.
It was around 35 times heavier than its close feathered relatives.
Despite its size it had a toothless beak and probably feathers.

description: One of the earliest dinosaurs of all, from a time when dinosaurs were still rare. This nimble predator had grasping hands and a special sliding jaw joint to grip struggling prey.
interestingFacts: It is one of the oldest known dinosaurs, over 230 million years old.
It lived when dinosaurs were still a small part of the animal world.
A flexible sliding jaw joint helped it hold onto wriggling prey.

description: A living tank covered head to tail in bony armour — even its eyelids were shielded with bone. A heavy club at the end of its tail could smash an attacker's legs.
interestingFacts: It was so well armoured that even its eyelids had bony shields.
Its tail ended in a heavy club of solid bone for swinging at predators.
It is one of the best-known armoured dinosaurs, with many skeletons found.

description: A spiky armoured dinosaur bristling with blade-like spikes along its sides and a shield of fused bone over its hips. It relied on armour, not speed, to survive.
interestingFacts: Rows of flat, blade-like spikes ran along each side of its body.
A shield of fused bony plates protected its hips.
Many individuals were found buried together in Utah.

description: A strange long-necked plant-eater with a wide, straight-edged mouth packed with hundreds of tiny teeth — like a living lawn-mower that grazed low plants.
interestingFacts: Its wide mouth held more than 500 tiny teeth arranged like a comb.
It replaced each tooth about once a month as they wore out.
Its skull was so full of air spaces it was almost see-through.

description: A powerful Jurassic hunter from England that holds a special place in history: it was the very first dinosaur ever given a scientific name.
interestingFacts: It was the first dinosaur ever scientifically named, back in 1824.
It was one of the fossils that inspired the invention of the word 'dinosaur'.
Early scientists wrongly pictured it as a giant four-legged lizard.

description: A sturdy plant-eater with a horny beak that could walk on two legs or drop to all fours to feed. It was an early relative of the famous Iguanodon.
interestingFacts: It was a close relative and forerunner of Iguanodon.
It could switch between walking on two legs and four.
It cropped plants with a toothless beak and chewed with cheek teeth.

description: One of the largest predators of the Jurassic, armed with long dagger-like teeth. It hunted across what is now North America and Europe.
interestingFacts: It was among the biggest meat-eaters of the entire Jurassic Period.
Fossils from Portugal make it one of Europe's largest known land predators.
It had exceptionally long, blade-like teeth for its size.

description: One of Australia's most complete dinosaurs, a big plant-eater with a strange hollow bump on its snout that may have been used to make loud honking calls.
interestingFacts: It is one of the most complete dinosaur skeletons ever found in Australia.
A hollow bump on its snout may have amplified its calls.
It could walk on two legs or four while browsing plants.

description: A medium-sized Spanish predator with a bizarre tall triangular hump in front of its hips, and bumps on its arms that hint it may have had quill-like structures.
interestingFacts: It had a strange tall, triangular hump rising just in front of its hips.
Bumps on its arm bones suggest it may have had quill-like feathers.
Its beautifully preserved skeleton was found in Spain.

description: The first meat-eating dinosaur ever discovered in Antarctica, sporting an odd crest that swept across its head above the eyes.
interestingFacts: It was the first meat-eating dinosaur found in Antarctica.
Its curled head crest earned it the nickname 'Elvisaurus'.
When it lived, Antarctica was warmer and covered in forests.

description: A bulldog-snouted predator from Madagascar with a single stubby horn on its head and tiny useless arms. It is one of the few dinosaurs with solid evidence it ate its own kind.
interestingFacts: It had a short, deep bulldog-like snout with a small horn on top.
Bite marks on its own bones are strong evidence that it was a cannibal.
Its arms were even shorter and more useless than those of T. rex.

description: A large tyrannosaur relative covered in shaggy feathers — the biggest feathered dinosaur ever found. It proved that even giant meat-eaters could be fuzzy.
interestingFacts: It is the largest dinosaur ever found with direct evidence of feathers.
Its body was covered in long, hair-like filament feathers.
It showed that big tyrannosaur relatives could be fluffy, not scaly.

description: One of the earliest and most primitive of the plated stegosaurs, from China. Unlike its later cousins, it still had small teeth at the front of its mouth.
interestingFacts: It is one of the oldest and most primitive stegosaurs known.
Unlike later stegosaurs, it kept small teeth at the front of its beak.
A pair of large spikes stuck out from its shoulders.

description: One of the earliest and most complete armoured dinosaurs, covered in rows of bony studs. It sits near the root of the family tree that led to Stegosaurus and Ankylosaurus.
interestingFacts: It is one of the earliest and most completely known armoured dinosaurs.
Rows of bony scutes ran along its back and sides for protection.
It was an early relative of both the plated and club-tailed armoured dinosaurs.

description: A small, speedy two-legged plant-eater built like a gazelle of the dinosaur world, darting away from danger on the ancient Isle of Wight.
interestingFacts: It was a small, fast runner that relied on speed to escape predators.
Scientists once wrongly believed it climbed trees like a modern bird.
Its ridged teeth sharpened themselves as it chewed tough plants.

description: A small bone-headed dinosaur with a thick, domed skull. A cousin of Pachycephalosaurus, it may have used its reinforced head for shoving contests or display.
interestingFacts: It had a thick, bony dome on top of its skull.
It was a smaller relative of the famous Pachycephalosaurus.
Its reinforced skull may have been used for head-shoving or display.

description: Possibly the earliest known dinosaur — or its closest cousin — from the Middle Triassic of Tanzania. Living around 245 million years ago, it pushes the dawn of the dinosaurs back by millions of years.
interestingFacts: It may be the oldest known dinosaur, living about 245 million years ago.
It is named after Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi), near where its bones were found in Tanzania.
Its fossils sat in a museum drawer for roughly 80 years before being identified in 2012.
